gaps.subject: DataPlanePlacement.awsAccountId
gaps.detail: Typed as `string | null` rather than a branded Id; the field name names Account. Declared intent: ⚠️ STAYS BARE (R1) — AWS mints it, and under BYOA it is minted in the CUSTOMER's account. Null for hosted. 🛑 THIS FIELD IS SUPPLIED BY THE CUSTOMER AND IS THE THING REGISTRATION MUST BE CHECKED AGAINST. A registration presenting a token minted for this placement, from an account that is not this one, is a redemption by the wrong party. Nothing here enforces that; the seam that redeems must.

gaps.subject: DataPlanePlacement.externalId

gaps.subject: AuditEvent.subjectId
gaps.detail: Typed as `string` rather than a branded Id. Declared intent: ⚠️ STAYS BARE (R4), AND `subjectType` IS WHY. The pair IS the identifier: an audit row names a row of ANY type, so no single brand is correct here and picking one would be worse than none. Identical in shape and reason to `ResourceRef.(resourceType, resourceId)` and to `DataAccessEvent`'s own pair — and the last of those is deliberate, because the two streams answer one question together and a divergence in this pair is what would break the join. Listed in `BareByRule` in `model/identity.ts`.

gaps.subject: AccessResourceGrant.nominatedSubjectIds
gaps.detail: Typed as `string[]` rather than a branded Id. Declared intent: ⚠️ STAYS BARE (R4), AND THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE IS THE ARGUMENT. It WAS `nominatedDocumentIds: SourceDocumentId[]` — branded, and wrong, because a branded enumeration could only ever name documents and an FDE needing one EXCEPTION had no delivery path. Widening it to bare ids is what fixed that. Re-branding it to any single type in this sweep would reinstate exactly the defect the widening removed. Listed in `BareByRule` in `model/identity.ts`.

gaps.subject: DataAccessEvent.subjectId

The pair `(subjectType, subjectId)` IS the identifier; a read row names a row of ANY type. The two streams answer *"who read this and who changed it"* together, and a divergence in this pair between them is what would break that join. Listed in `BareByRule` in `model/identity.ts`.
